thread:
maria-support: Hi @customer-acme — sorry you're hitting this. You said you can't find any request IDs in your logs after the 401s. Can you confirm whether you're behind a gateway/proxy?
customer-acme: yes, requests go through our api-gw (kong) + an internal edge. the SDK call just returns 401 and no headers we can see.
maria-support: OK. Most likely the proxy is stripping the tracing headers. We need either the raw upstream headers or a client-side trace. Two quick options: 1) capture a HAR from the browser or a tcp dump on the client, or 2) get the SDK debug log showing the outgoing headers.
customer-acme: how do we get SDK debug logs? running node on serverless.
maria-support: In the Node SDK set env var RW_DEBUG=1 and capture stdout. It will log the final request headers and the x-rw-trace token (if present). Example: `RW_DEBUG=1 node ./app.js` — then paste the log lines that look like `Outgoing request headers:` and `x-rw-trace:`.
jon-eng: if the gateway is terminating headers, ask them to check `proxy_set_header`/`preserve_host` or similar config. Also ask them to send a minimal curl that reproduces the 401 so we can see what their public-facing response contains.
customer-acme: attaching curl now — `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.acme.example/v1/generate` returns 401 and in verbose I only see `www-authenticate` and no x-request-id.
maria-support: Perfect — that shows the gateway didn't forward our `x-rw-debug`/`x-rw-trace`. Can you run curl with the Redwood SDK header override so we can correlate? Example curl to reproduce and give us the request id we expect from Redwood side:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.acme.example/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \ 
  -H "x-client-id: acme-web" \ 
  -H "x-requested-with: XMLHttpRequest" \ 
  -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
And from your gateway logs please grep for `x-rw-trace` or `x-request-id`. If none, gateway is stripping.
customer-acme: gateway logs show no x-rw-trace. They strip unknown headers by default.
maria-support: Ok, next best is to ask them to include a response header back with our trace token. We can also ask you to enable our debug-token in the SDK call so the SDK prints the debug token before proxy. In Node SDK: `client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, debug: true})` then call and paste console output.
ops-oncall: If they can't change the gateway, we can also search our ingress logs by IP + approximate timestamp. Ask for a sample client IP and a short time window. We can search and return matching request IDs.
customer-acme: IP is 198.51.100.12, failing requests between 2025-04-22T15:12:00Z and 15:14:00Z.
john-eng: (typo, meant jon-eng) I'll run a log search now.
debug-bot: Search started for ip=198.51.100.12 start=2025-04-22T15:12:00Z end=2025-04-22T15:14:00Z — returning 2 matches with internal_trace_ids: `rwd-0001a7` and `rwd-0001a8` — forwarding to eng.
jon-eng: Got traces. `rwd-0001a7` corresponds to a 401 with `auth-service` upstream rejecting token. Sending a repro checklist to @customer-acme: 1) paste the SDK debug output or HAR; 2) attach one curl -v of the failing request; 3) confirm client IP + exact timestamps; 4) (optional) temporarily allow `x-rw-trace` through gateway for 10 minutes so we can correlate live.
customer-acme: will send SDK output and the curl. also can open a short maintenance window to allow header passthrough.
maria-support: thanks — once we have the SDK debug block and the curl we can close the loop. If you want, follow this minimal HAR capture guide: 1) open Chrome DevTools -> Network -> right click -> Save HAR with content; 2) find the POST to `/v1/generate` and send that file to us. We only need the single entry.
jon-eng: For internal notes: if proxies strip headers frequently, we should add a troubleshooting snippet in support KB showing header names to ask for (x-rw-trace, x-request-id, x-rw-debug) plus a one-line grep for common gateways: `grep -i "x-rw" /var/log/nginx/access.log`
maria-support: Great. I'll wait for the HAR / SDK output. :thumbsup:
customer-acme: Uploaded SDK log snippet: `Outgoing request headers: { host: 'api.redwood.ai', 'authorization': 'Bearer ***', 'x-client-id': 'acme-web', 'x-rw-trace': 'rwd-0001a7' }` — looks like SDK set the header but gateway still didn't forward.
maria-support: That confirms it. Jon, ops — recommend they temporarily allow the header or we accept our IP search as sufficient.
ops-oncall: We can accept the IP+trace match and escalate to account team for guidance on gateway config.
maria-support: Thanks everyone — transferring to account manager to coordinate the gateway change. Closing notes: attach the two trace ids `rwd-0001a7`, `rwd-0001a8`, the SDK snippet, and the curl to the support ticket.
